MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Food Services Assistant | Buderim Hospital 

Employment Term:CasualOpportunitiesAvailable

Located in: Buderim Private Hospital, Sunshine Coast QLD

Remuneration:$37.36p-hr(incl Casual Loading)+ Super + NFP Salary Packaging (save tax and increase your take home pay)

Applications will be reviewed as they arereceived, andtherefore may result in theroleclosing early if the right applicant is found.

Make a meaningful difference with Buderim Private Hospital

As one of the Sunshine Coast's largest hospitals, we provide a comprehensive range of surgical and medical services using the latest technology. This includes emergency, maternity, intensive care, cardiovascular, obstetric andgynaecology, urology, cancer care, general medicine, renal and respiratory services,orthopaedicand mental health care, among many others. With a deep connection to the Sunshine Coast that's 40 years in the making, Buderim Private Hospital partners with our patients to deliverpersonalisedone-on-one care from the heart and make a meaningful difference in people's lives.

An integral part of our team, as aFood Services Assistant, you'll be encouragedto grow, develop and feel empowered to make the everyday easier for the people we care so passionately about. Let's make a meaningful difference, together! 

Your part in our Buderim Hospital team

As part of our Food Services team, you willbe responsible forproviding high-quality service delivery to all customers including patients,staffand visitors. You willbe responsible forbasic meal preparation, portioning and serving of hot and cold meals, meal delivery and distribution, and cleaning. In addition to this you will: 

Assist with the timely assembly, delivery and collection of meals to patients and work collaboratively with clinical staff to ensure all patients with special dietary requirements-changes are addressed and met 

Act as quality control to ensure all meals are presented to a high standard and are appropriate for each patient, escalating issues where required 

Ensure a high standard of hygiene and safety throughout the food services department that complies with the hospital food safety program 

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of HACCP principles in accordance with the hospital's food safety program

What makes a difference for us?

Flexibility to work across all shifts - mornings, afternoons, evenings, and weekends 

Previousexperience in a food service or hospitality team environment, preferably within the Healthcare industry.

Demonstrated understanding and competencies in manual handling training, chemical use,hand hygieneand food safety 

Ability to work well in a team and support a positive team environment 

Basic numeracy, literacy, verbalcommunicationand interpersonal skills including ability to read, measure accurately and perform basic math skills 

Willingness to obtain required vaccinations in line with hospitals infection control requirements, as well as undergo national criminal history check and functionalassessment

What makes a difference for you? 

NFP Salary Packaging: Save tax and increase your take home pay by salary packaging your everyday living expenses and bills (up to $15,900) and meal entertainment (up to $2,650) per annum. To learn more about this benefit watch the video via the following link: Salary Packaging Explained

Flexible work arrangements to support work-life balance 

A recognition and rewards platform, providing employee discounts at hundreds of retailers, including everyday expenses, holidays, health insurance, annual awards celebration, wellbeing and employee assistance programs 

12 weeks paid parental leave and 2 weeks paid partner leave, available after 6 months service, in addition to the government scheme 

Diversity and inclusive leave, offering paid gender affirmation leave and cultural leave options (paid and unpaid) for those who may celebrate Lunar New Year, Diwali, Ramadan, NAIDOC weeks and other significant cultural events 

Career development opportunities to challenge yourself, grow and make a meaningful difference 

A positive and inclusive team based on respect, shared standards, strong values and a commitment to serving others 

We'd love you to be part of our UnitingCare family 

By joining our Hospitals, you'll also be welcomed as part of the UnitingCare family. The second-largest Queensland employer, we're a proud not-for-profit with more than 17,500 staff and 9, 000 volunteers across our brands of BlueCare, Lifeline, ARRCS, The Wesley Hospital, Buderim Private Hospital, St Stephen's Hospital, and St Andrew's War Memorial Hospital, and have been leading by example for more than 100 years. Our team are compassionate, inclusive and committed to the work we do, helping people live life in all its fullness. 

Child safe, Child friendly 

UnitingCare is committed to being a Child Safe, Child Friendly organisation and will: 

provide welcoming, safe and nurturing services for children 

implement measures to prevent child abuse and neglect within our services 

appropriately and immediately address child abuse and neglect if it does occur 

abide by the Child Safe Standards and adhere to the Reportable Conduct Scheme 

Diversity & Inclusion 

Our approach is simple - everybody is welcome here. At UnitingCare, diversity is at the core of our who we are, our mission and our values. We are committed to providing equal opportunities to all employees no matter their sex, race, culture, sexual orientation, disability or gender identity. Demonstrating our commitment to reconciliation and building long-term employment opportunities for First Nations peoples, UnitingCare strongly encourages Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants for this position. 

Safe workplace 

We work hard to make our services welcoming and safe for every person. We are united in keeping children, young people and the elderly safe from harm, within our services, workplaces and the communities we support. We are committed to speaking up loudly for their safety. 

Commitment to Safeguarding

We are committed in creating services and workplaces that are welcoming and safe for every person. We work together to protect children, young people, adults and the elderly from harm within our services and the communities we support. We speak up for their safety to ensure their voices are heard. Our recruitment and workplace practices reflect our dedication in preventing abuse, harm and exploitation across UnitingCare.    Click here to Apply now →

Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network.



Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.

Help shape the future of healthcare at Monash Health and embark on a rewarding career where your dedication makes a difference in people's lives.


About the Role


Join our team as a Food Services Assistant on a part time, ongoing to work at Kingston centre. In this role, you will be guided under the leadership of the Food Services Manager and working with the broader Support Services team.



FSAs play a vital role in providing high-quality meal services to patients and supporting overall patient nutrition and food safety. FSAs are responsible for the preparation and delivery of meals, cleaning of food service areas, all whilst ensuring patient's dietary needs are met accurately and efficiently. FSAs contribute to patient care by ensuring meals are delivered on time, safely, accurately and with respect.


Key responsibilities include, but not limited to:



Delivering and collecting meal trays and Burlodge trolleys to and from service areas


Regenerating and preparing meals in line with production and clinical needs, including special functions


Cleaning and sanitising food trays, food preparation areas, and kitchen equipment


Operating dishwashers and other food service equipment safely and efficiently


Restocking pantries and trolleys; whilst maintaining food stock levels as required


Completing all food safety and cleaning documentation accurately and in a timely manner



We currently have the following opportunities available: 




Position 1 - Ward Food Services


Days and Time: 


Wednesday: 7:30 am - 2:30 pm


Thursday: 7:30 am - 2:30 pm


Friday: 7:30 am - 1:30 pm


Please note that the successful applicantmust be available to work all three morning shifts: Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. Availability for all three shifts is an essential requirement of this position one.



Position 2 - Ward Food Services


Day and time: Sunday: 2:00 pm - 7:30 pm



About You


To ensure your success in this role, you will bring experience in food services within a hospital, aged care, or hospitality setting with strong demonstrated knowledge of food safety standards and hygiene standards. You have a passion for patient care and nutrition, ensuring patients are treated with respect and empathy. You are a reliable and punctual team member with great verbal and written communication skills; and intermediate computer skills. Whether you work independently or as part of a team; you always follow manual handling, safety protocols, and procedural instructions. It would be an advantage if you also have comprehensive understanding of diet codes, texture modified foods and fluids, food allergies and intolerances.


You are also required to hold a HLTFSE001: Follow basic food safety practices or SITXFSA001: Use hygienic practices for food safety.



Why you will love working with us


As an FSA, you will play a vital role in supporting patient care while working within a supportive and inclusive team culture. Monash Health offers ongoing opportunities for professional development and leadership training. FSAs benefit from job stability within Victoria's largest public health service, along with clear career pathways across support services. 


As a Monash Health employee you will enjoy a variety of benefits, such as:



Salary packaging options to increase your take-home pay


Novated leasing for vehicle options


Full-time employees accrue 5 week's annual leave (pro rata for part-time employees)

About the Department - Program


The Support Services team is a collaborative and dedicated group that plays a crucial role in maintaining a safe, clean, and welcoming environment for patients, visitors, and staff. Our culture is built on respect, compassion, and excellence, and we are committed to continuous improvement and professional development.



About Kingston Centre: 


Kingston Centre is a specialist healthcare facility in Melbourne's south-east, operated by Monash Health, that focuses on rehabilitation, aged care and ongoing recovery. It provides a wide range of services including sub-acute care, aged mental health, residential aged care and allied health, helping patients regain independence and improve their quality of life. The centre also offers specialised clinics and programs-such as dementia, falls and movement disorder services-supporting both older adults and people recovering from illness or injury.

Requisition ID: REQ673099
Located in: Maitland Hospital
Applications Close: Sunday the 19th of July
*Tentative Interviews the week of 20th

 

A chance to shape the Future of Surgical Services and make a lasting impact.

This is more than a leadership role - it's an opportunity to influence the future of one of the fastest-growing hospitals in NSW.

As a result of significant growth across surgical services, Hunter New England Health is creating a brand-new Operational Nurse Manager position. This newly established role offers the unique opportunity to make your mark, drive innovation, and lead the continued evolution of surgical services at Maitland Hospital.

If you're an experienced nursing leader who thrives on strategic thinking, operational excellence, and leading high-performing teams through change, we'd love to hear from you.

 

About the Role

Reporting to the senior leadership team, you'll provide both strategic and operational leadership across a broad portfolio including:

Surgical inpatient services

Orthopaedic and General Surgery

Surgical outpatient services

Elective surgery coordination and waitlist oversight

Specialist nursing services
 

Partnering and working collaboratively with the executive, medical and multidisciplinary teams, you'll ensure exceptional patient outcomes while delivering safe, efficient and sustainable services aligned with Hunter New England Health's strategic direction.

What You'll Be Doing

You will:

Lead operational planning and service delivery across Surgical Services

Drive innovation and continuous improvement initiatives

Ensure outstanding clinical governance, patient safety and quality outcomes

Oversee workforce planning, financial performance and resource management

Build and mentor high-performing multidisciplinary teams including orthopaedics, general surgical, speciality nurses and outpatient teams.

Partner with clinical leaders to improve patient flow, elective surgery performance and service outcomes

Influence the future direction of surgical services within a rapidly expanding facility.

About You

We're seeking a motivated, experienced and resilient nursing leader who brings:

Current registration as a Registered Nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia and a postgraduate qualification in a relevant specialty area is desirable, and-or demonstrated relevant leadership or management experience 

Proven leadership experience managing large clinical teams

Experience within surgical services, ideally including Orthopaedics or General Surgery

A strategic mindset with the ability to balance operational demands with long-term service planning

Demonstrated experience leading change and driving innovation

Strong clinical governance, quality improvement and stakeholder engagement skills

Experience managing budgets, workforce planning and service performance

Experience with elective surgery and surgical waitlist management is highly desirable.

Why Join Maitland Hospital?

Maitland Hospital is one of New South Wales's newest and fastest-growing health facilities, purpose-built to deliver world-class healthcare in a modern, state-of-the-art environment. With contemporary clinical spaces, advanced technology and ongoing investment in services, the hospital provides an exceptional setting for both patients and staff.

This is a rare opportunity to:

Join a growing hospital at an exciting stage of expansion

Step into a newly created leadership position and shape its direction

Influence how surgical services evolve for the future

Work alongside an engaged and supportive executive leadership team

Drive meaningful improvements that directly impact patient care and clinical outcomes

Enjoy excellent professional development and career progression opportunities within Hunter New England Health

If you're ready to lead with purpose, inspire change and leave a lasting impact on one of NSW's most exciting health services, we'd love to hear from you.

 

Apply today and help shape the future of Surgical Services at Maitland Hospital.

Additional Information

To be eligible for permanent employment in this position you must be an Australian Citizen, or a permanent resident of Australia, or a New Zealand citizen with a current New Zealand Passport. Employment of a temporary visa holder may only occur if no suitable local candidate is identified for the position; in this instance, you may only be offered employment in line with the conditions and expiry date of your visa.

We are unable to accommodate visa sponsorship for applicants requiring a visa for this position.

All new employees must agree to comply with the requirements outlined in the policy.
